# Navigation

For the demo app, README.md supersedes the route table, launcher and per-board figures; this file still gives links, shells and seed values.

Information architecture, shells, every route and every link of the Palakat prototype. 19 November 2026. `CONVENTIONS.md` is fixed and wins over this file; the board source wins on what a screen shows. Section 2 and section 3 were generated by a script that read `canvas.json`, `board-manifest.json`, every board source (including the links its logic class builds, found by running each logic class through all its tweaks and reachable states) and the **Route** line of every spec in `screens/`.

Contents: 1 Shells · 2 Route table · 3 Link graph · 4 Launcher · 5 Back, deep links and unknown routes.

## Quick reference

- One route per board: `/<Stem>`. Child routes (`/<Stem>/<sub>`) are listed per board in section 2; the screen spec defines them.
- Every control that opens another board is `Tautan(ke: '<Stem>', cara: …)`. Four kinds, used in the tables below:

| Kind | `cara` | What it does | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| push | `Cara.dorong` (default) | `context.push('/X')` | Drill-ins: everything that is not one of the three below |
| go | `Cara.ganti` | `context.go('/X')` | Side-nav items, phone tab-bar items, and the links section 3 marks go, all taken from the screen specs: shortcuts to a side-nav or tab-level page (WebBeranda's "+ Pendapatan" → WebTransaksi), signing in ("Buka Beranda"), signing out or a session ending ("Masuk", "Masuk lagi", "Keluar"), and "finish and return home" actions (BantuanAI's "Simpan sebagai draf" → Main) |
| up | `Cara.naik` | `kembaliKe('/X')`: pop when the page directly below is `/X` or a child of `/X`, otherwise `go('/X')` | Phone back arrows, web breadcrumbs, links labelled "Kembali …", and the "return to where you came from" actions the specs name (for example "Pakai …", "Batalkan" on BukaNama) |
| self | none | Nothing (the board is already open). If the screen spec gives the control an in-board effect, the screen does that instead | Links to the board itself: active side-nav items, BerandaJabatan's and KeuanganUnit's header arrows, rows without a target |

- Where a screen spec says push or go for a specific link, it agrees with section 3 (section 3 took those choices over). If a spec is edited later and disagrees, the spec wins for its own board.
- Shells are the `components.md` widgets each screen includes: `PonselTabBar` (4.2), `KepalaPonsel` (4.1), `NavSamping` inside `HalamanWeb` (4.3, 4.4). The device frame `BingkaiPerangkat` and the Keadaan panel `PanelKeadaan` sit outside the router's navigator (5.2). Page transitions are `motion.md`'s (5.3).

## 1. Shells

Five kinds of frame: the phone finance tab bar (2 boards), the phone header with a back arrow (most phone boards), the web side nav in six variants (86 laptop and tablet boards), the tablet layout of the side nav (3 boards), and no shell at all (8 A4 pages, 4 sheets). The platform boards of rounds 2 to 5 use the same phone header and the web variant `navPlatform` (1.5).

### 1.1 Phone finance tab bar

Drawn on exactly two boards (no other board has a bottom tab bar, `TutupBuku` included):

- **Main**, only while its view is Beranda (`/Main`) or Transaksi (`/Main/transaksi`) (`showNav: s.screen === 'beranda' || s.screen === 'daftar'`). Active item: Beranda on `/Main`, Transaksi on `/Main/transaksi`. Hidden on `/Main/catat`, `/Main/mata-anggaran`, `/Main/periksa`, `/Main/detail`.
- **Lainnya**, only on its hub view (`/Lainnya`). Active item: Lainnya. Its inner views (`/Lainnya/kas`, `/Lainnya/aturan`, `/Lainnya/riwayat`) use the phone header with back instead.

Geometry (board CSS): pinned to the bottom of the 390 × 844 screen, height 84, `permukaan`, top border 1 `garis`, five equal columns, items aligned to the top, padding-top 8. Each item: min height 52, column, centred, gap 3, 13/600, icon 22 × 22 (24 box, stroke 2, round caps), colour `laut` when active and `tinta3` otherwise. The centre item is a circle: `laut` field, 4 px `kertas` ring, lifted 22 px above the bar (`margin-top: -22px`), plus icon 24 (stroke 2.4, `diLaut`), Semantics label "Catat transaksi". On Main it is a `<button>` 58 × 58 outside measure (ring included); on Lainnya it is a link with `box-sizing: content-box`, so 58 inside plus the ring (66 outside). Each board keeps its own size.

| # | Label | Icon (24 box) | On Main | On Lainnya |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Beranda | path `M4 11l8-7 8 7v9H4z` (round joins) | In-board (`keBeranda`): pop to `/Main` | `Tautan(ke: 'Main', cara: Cara.ganti)` |
| 2 | Transaksi | path `M5 7h14M5 12h14M5 17h9` | In-board (`bukaDaftar`): `/Main/transaksi` (01-main.md) | `Tautan(ke: 'Main', cara: Cara.ganti)` (the board links to Main's Beranda view, not to Transaksi) |
| 3 | (Catat, icon only) | path `M12 5v14M5 12h14` | In-board (`bukaSheet`): opens the Catat bottom sheet, not a route | `Tautan(ke: 'Main', cara: Cara.ganti)` (opens Main at Beranda; the sheet does not open) |
| 4 | Bulan | rect 4,5 16 × 15 rx 3 + path `M4 10h16M9 3v4M15 3v4` | `Tautan(ke: 'TutupBuku', cara: Cara.ganti)` | `Tautan(ke: 'TutupBuku', cara: Cara.ganti)` |
| 5 | Lainnya | three filled dots r 2 at x 5, 12, 19 | `Tautan(ke: 'Lainnya', cara: Cara.ganti)` | Active; a plain label, not a link |

`TutupBuku` (the Bulan tab) draws no tab bar and no back control on its Bulan view, so the way out is system or browser Back (section 5). On web, browser Back returns to the page the tab was pressed on; on Android, system Back returns to the launcher, because `go` replaced the stack. That is what CONVENTIONS asks for ("go for a tab change").

### 1.2 Phone header with back

Shared by every phone board below. Geometry (board source): row, centred, gap 8, padding 14 12 8. Back link 44 × 44, centred chevron 22 (path `M15 6l-6 6 6 6`, stroke 2, round caps, `tinta`), no visible text, Semantics label from the board's `aria-label` ("Kembali ke …"). Then a column that fills the rest: h1 18/700, optional subtitle 13 `tinta2`. On boards with `jabatanKosong`, the one-line PitaJabatanKosong strip sits above the header. The back link is always kind **up**: `KepalaPonsel(kembaliKe: 'Lainnya', labelKembali: 'Kembali ke Lainnya')` builds `Tautan(ke: 'Lainnya', cara: Cara.naik)`.

Back arrows that change the board's own view (for example TutupBuku's Cek view, Kewajiban's case view) are not links: they pop the child route or change state, as each spec says.

No back control to another board (system Back only): TutupBuku, Awal, Terbatas, Pemeriksa, Masuk, PilihBulan. Main and Lainnya carry the tab bar instead. BerandaJabatan and KeuanganUnit draw the header arrow but it links to the board itself (kind **self**; see 14-berandajabatan.md and 23-alurunit.md for what it does in-board).

### 1.3 Web side nav

Every laptop board (and the three tablet boards) draws the same side-nav frame with one of six item lists. Geometry, from the boards' shared CSS:

- Page root: at least the window height, a row that wraps, `kertas`, `tinta`, sans 15/1.45 (`isiWeb`).
- Nav: `flex: 1 1 220px` (220 wide in practice), padding 24 16, `permukaan`, right border 1 `garis`, column, gap 20.
- Brand: row, gap 10, padding 0 8. Mark 26 × 26 (rect 2,2 20 × 20 rx 6, stroke 2 `laut`, dash 3 3; right half path `M12 2h4a6 6 0 0 1 6 6v8a6 6 0 0 1-6 6h-4z` filled `laut`), then "palakat" 700 18/1.1 over "Jemaat Karunia" 13 `tinta3`.
- Items: stacked with no gap; each a link, min height 44, padding 0 12, radius 10, 600, no underline. Active item: `tinta` field, `permukaan` text. Others: transparent, `tinta` text. Every item is a `go`; the active item usually points at the board itself (kind **self**), but on a drill-in page it points at the section's main page (WebBukti's active "Laporan" opens WebPaketLaporan).
- Footer: pushed to the bottom (`margin-top: auto`), padding 12 8 0, top border 1 `garis`, 13 `tinta2`; names in bold `tinta`. Text per board in the footer table below.
- Main column: `flex: 999 1 560px`, min width 0, padding 28 `clamp(16px, 3vw, 40px)` 40, column; the gap is per board (spec).
- **860 px and below** (`@media (max-width:860px)`): the nav becomes a full-width top bar: row that wraps, centred, gap 0 12, padding 8 16, no right border, bottom border 1 `garis`. A toggle appears at the right end: min height 44, padding 0 16, radius 14, border 1.5 `tinta`, `permukaan`, 700 14, label "Menu"; when open it turns `tinta` with `permukaan` text and reads "Tutup menu". The items and the footer are hidden until it is open; then the items show as a full-width block (padding 8 0) and the footer below them (margin-top 0, padding-bottom 8). The toggle is a checkbox on the board (`aria-label="Menu"`): build it as a toggle button with Semantics label "Menu" and a toggled state. It starts closed on every page.

Widget: `NavSamping(item: navKeuangan, aktif: 1, pengguna: …)` (components.md 4.3). The six item lists below are consts in `lib/shell/nav_item.dart` under the names given here; a screen passes one by name (the link test relies on that), the index of its active item, and its footer (which may depend on `jabatanKosong` or a tweak). Each item is a `Tautan(…, cara: Cara.ganti)`.

#### Variants

**`navKeuangan`** (7 items, 52 boards): Beranda → `/WebBeranda` · Transaksi → `/WebTransaksi` · Uang Muka dan Titipan → `/WebKewajiban` · Rekonsiliasi → `/WebRekonsiliasi` · Bulan dan tutup buku → `/WebTutupBuku` · Laporan → `/WebPaketLaporan` · Pengaturan → `/WebPengaturan`

**`navTerbatas`** (3 items, 1 board): Beranda → `/WebTerbatas` · Transaksi → `/WebTerbatas` · Laporan → `/WebTerbatas`

**`navMasuk`** (1 item, 1 board): Masuk → `/WebMasuk`

**`navVerifikasi`** (1 item, 1 board): Verifikasi wewenang → `/WebVerifikasi`

**`navPemulihan`** (2 items, 1 board): Masuk → `/WebMasuk` · Pemulihan akun → `/WebPemulihan`

**`navPlatform`** (10 items, 30 boards): Beranda → `/WebBerandaJabatan` · Keuangan → `/WebBeranda` · Dokumen gereja → `/WebDokumenGereja` · Pengumuman → `/WebPengumuman` · Warta Jemaat → `/WebWartaArsip` · Data jemaat → `/WebDataAnggota` · Ibadah dan kegiatan → `/Ibadah` · Panitia → `/Panitia` · Pemberitahuan → `/WebKotakMasuk` · Pengaturan → `/WebPenugasan`

`navTerbatas` points all three items at WebTerbatas itself (kind **self**). `navPemulihan` marks "Masuk" active even on WebPemulihan; copy that. `navPlatform` sends "Ibadah dan kegiatan" and "Panitia" to the phone boards Ibadah and Panitia (no laptop layout exists for those posts, decision 26); they open in the phone frame.

AIBulan (a phone board) defines the `navKeuangan` list in its logic class but never draws it. The manifest still lists those seven targets as its `jsLinks`; they are dead and are left out of this file's graph (section 3.2).

### 1.4 Tablet

TabBeranda, TabTransaksi and TabCatat are drawn 834 wide, which is below 860, so their side nav is always the collapsed top bar with "Menu" (1.3). They use `navKeuangan` with the finance footer; active item Beranda (TabBeranda) or Transaksi (TabTransaksi, TabCatat). They have no tablet-to-tablet links: every link opens a laptop board (WebTransaksi, WebCatat, …), which then renders fluid at the same window width. TabBeranda is reached only from PetaLayar ("Lebar tablet") and the launcher; TabTransaksi and TabCatat only from the launcher. In the prototype they render as fluid pages like laptop boards (CONVENTIONS, Form factors); at a window wider than 860 the nav would expand, which is fine.

### 1.5 Platform navigation (rounds 2 to 5)

Row cards on BerandaJabatan, KotakMasuk, CariOrang and AntreanVerifikasi are built in the logic class with a helper `hal(n)`: on a phone board it returns `n`; on a web board (`web = true`) it keeps `n` when `n` is one of 26 phone-only boards (AlurAnggota, AlurBeranda, AlurDana, AlurIbadah, AlurModul, AlurNama, AlurPanitia, AlurPanitiaBaru, AlurPelimpahan, AlurPenugasan, AlurPeristiwa, AntreanVerifikasi, CabutIzin, Ibadah, Kehadiran, KeuanganUnit, KonfirmasiKeluarga, Modul, Panitia, Pelimpahan, PemberiPersetujuan, Peristiwa, PermintaanDana, PermohonanAnggota, PersembahanSaya, TampilanNama), maps `Main` to `WebBeranda`, and otherwise prefixes `Web`. The same holds on the phone: Main has no link to BerandaJabatan. This is how the boards are drawn; do not add a link.

Finance boards drawn in rounds 2 to 5 sit in the finance frame: KeuanganUnit (unit finance, phone; its arrow links to itself), PermintaanDana (back to KeuanganUnit), AlurDana (back to PermintaanDana), SelesaikanUnit and Kesiapan (back to TutupBuku), PersembahanBernama and AlurUnit (back to Main, "Kembali ke Keuangan"), KasUnit (back to Lainnya, "Kembali ke Pengaturan"), AlurPengembalian (back to Pengembalian); on the laptop, `navPlatform` boards with "Keuangan" active are WebAlurPengembalian, WebJabatanKosong, WebSelesaikanUnit, WebPersembahanBernama, WebAlurUnit, WebKasUnit; WebKesiapan uses `navKeuangan` instead.

### 1.7 A4 pages and sheets (no shell)

- **A4 pages** (A4F01, A4F02a, A4F02b, A4F02c, A4F14, A4Sementara, A4Terbatas, A4Warta): no app chrome and no links out. A fixed white page (794 × 1123, or 1123 × 794 for the three F02 pages) centred on `kertas`, scaled down to fit narrower windows, scrolling. Leaving is by Back. Reached by push from: A4F01 ← TutupBuku, WebTutupBuku, WebLaporan, WebPaketLaporan, Laporan, PetaLayar, Cakupan, Keputusan; A4F02a ← launcher only; A4F02b ← Keputusan; A4F02c ← Keputusan; A4F14 ← launcher only; A4Sementara ← launcher only; A4Terbatas ← Terbatas, WebTerbatas; A4Warta ← PetaPlatform, WartaEditor, WebWartaEditor.
- **Sheets** (PetaLayar 1760 × 1860, Cakupan 1400 × 1660, Keputusan 1280 × 1320, PetaPlatform 1280 × 2100): fixed size, scroll both ways, no app chrome. Their links are push, so Back returns to the sheet. PetaLayar is reached from Keputusan; the other three only from the launcher.

## 2. Route table

### 2.1 Router structure

`lib/router.dart` is generated by `prototype/tool/gen_boards.py` (CONVENTIONS). Shape:

```dart
GoRouter(
  initialLocation: '/',
  errorBuilder: (context, state) => TidakDitemukanScreen(lokasi: state.uri.toString()),
  routes: [
    GoRoute(path: '/', builder: (_, __) => const Peluncur(), routes: [
      GoRoute(path: '_komponen', builder: …),            // M1 gallery
      GoRoute(path: 'WebBeranda', pageBuilder: (c, s) => halaman(c, s, const WebBerandaScreen())),
      GoRoute(path: 'Cari', pageBuilder: (c, s) => halaman(c, s, const CariScreen(), kerangka: Kerangka.masuk)),
      // … one GoRoute per board without child routes …
      ShellRoute(                                           // one per board in the `json child-routes` block (2.2)
        builder: (_, __, child) => MainKendali(child: child), // owns the board state and LayarPonsel (strip, tab bar, toast, sheet)
        routes: [GoRoute(path: 'Main', pageBuilder: (c, s) => halaman(c, s, const MainScreen(), kerangka: Kerangka.masuk), routes: [
          GoRoute(path: 'transaksi', pageBuilder: (c, s) => halaman(c, s, MainScreen(anak: 'transaksi', param: s.pathParameters),
              kerangka: Kerangka.pudar, lama: const Duration(milliseconds: 200), kurva: Curves.ease)),
          GoRoute(path: 'catat', pageBuilder: (c, s) => halaman(c, s, MainScreen(anak: 'catat', param: s.pathParameters),
              kerangka: Kerangka.masuk, lama: const Duration(milliseconds: 280), kurva: PalakatMotion.keluar)), // …
        ])],
      ),
    ]),
  ],
)
```

- Every board route is a sub-route of the launcher `/`, so the launcher is always the bottom page: a board opened by `go` or by a deep link has the launcher below it, and Back from it returns there. Paths stay `/<Stem>`.
- A board with child routes is wrapped in a `ShellRoute` whose builder creates the board's state controller (`ChangeNotifier`) and disposes it, and its timers, when the last page of that board leaves the stack. The parent and child pages read the same state (02-awal.md, 10-aifoto.md). The child routes are those in the table, taken from the specs; the generator reads them from the `json child-routes` block at the end of 2.2.
- `<snake_stem>` in every import and screen path is `re.sub(r'(?<=[a-z0-9])(?=[A-Z])|(?<=[A-Z])(?=[A-Z][a-z])', '_', stem).lower()`, the same rule as the M0 stubs (README, M0 step 4): `AIFoto` → `ai_foto.dart`, `WebAI` → `web_ai.dart`, `A4F02a` → `a4_f02a.dart`.
- Naming convention for a board with child routes (the generator relies on it; the M0 stubs define both):
  - The board's screen file `lib/screens/<pageId>/<snake_stem>.dart` defines `class <Stem>Kendali extends StatefulWidget { const <Stem>Kendali({super.key, required this.child}); final Widget child; }`. Its state creates the board controller and disposes it. The `ShellRoute` builder is `(_, __, child) => <Stem>Kendali(child: child)`.
  - The same file's `<Stem>Screen` takes `{String? anak, Map<String, String> param = const {}}`. The board root route `/<Stem>` builds `const <Stem>Screen()` (`anak` null: the board's first view). A child route builds `<Stem>Screen(anak: '<jalur>', param: state.pathParameters)`, with `<jalur>` exactly as the `json child-routes` block writes it, path parameters included (`anak: 'kasus/:id'`, and `param['id']` holds the value).
  - The child route's page transition comes from its block entry: `halaman(c, s, …, kerangka: Kerangka.<masuk>, lama: Duration(milliseconds: <ms>), kurva: <kurva>)`, where `kurva` `"keluar"` is `PalakatMotion.keluar` and `"ease"` is `Curves.ease` (motion.md, easing table). An entry with `"masuk": null` gets `halaman(c, s, …)` with no `kerangka`, a `NoTransitionPage`.
- For every board with child routes, `<Stem>Kendali` owns LayarPonsel (strip, overlays); child pages are views only. All 17 such boards are phone boards (2.2), so the nested navigator sits inside LayarPonsel's Stack and page transitions never move the strip, tab bar, toast or sheet (01-main.md, Shell).
- **Re-entering a board with child routes.** A push whose target board has child routes and is already in the stack does `kembaliKe('/<Stem>')` and then resets that board's state to its initial state (the board remounts on the canvas). Because the target is known to be in the stack, this `kembaliKe` pops down to the page `/<Stem>` itself, the board's own child-route pages included (01-main.md's "pop to `/Main`"); it never stops after one pop and never falls back to `go`, so the pages beneath the board stay. `Tautan` does it (5.1). Reason: a `ShellRoute` has one fixed `navigatorKey`, so a plain push either reuses the shell already in the stack (the new page lands inside it, under the pages above, and cannot be seen) or builds a second shell with the same `GlobalKey` and throws. Cases on the boards: Cari pushed from `/Main/transaksi`, whose result rows push `/Main`; Sambungan → Main; BerandaJabatan, KotakMasuk and CariOrang → Main once Main is below; Keluar → Bendahara. A board without child routes is a plain `GoRoute`; pushing it again adds a second page, as before.
- **Reset.** While mounted, each `<Stem>Kendali` state registers a reset callback under its stem in a static map `ulangPapan` (stem → callback) and removes it on dispose, so an entry means "this board has child routes and is in the stack". The callback cancels the board's timers, puts the controller's state back to the board's initial state object (LayarPonsel's sheet and toast included) and increments a `generasi` counter that the Kendali provides along with the controller. The generator wraps the `<Stem>Screen(…)` of each of the board's routes in a small widget that reads `generasi` and returns `KeyedSubtree(key: ValueKey(generasi), child: screen)`, so widget-local state (text fields, scroll offsets) remounts as well. Tweak values in `PrototypeState` are kept. No transition runs: the pops are instant (5.3).
- Decision: keep `ShellRoute` with the two rules above. The alternative, nested `GoRoute`s without a shell plus a reference-counted controller per stem, is not used: a second push would still put two copies of the board on the stack sharing one state, which the canvas never shows.
- `halaman(context, state, child, kerangka: …)` is `motion.md`'s page builder (`lib/motion/halaman.dart`), keyed by `state.pageKey`; the generator passes `kerangka: Kerangka.masuk` for phone boards and nothing for other forms (5.3).
- Stems are case-sensitive (`/main` is unknown).

#### Child routes (input for `gen_boards.py`)

The 31 child routes of the 17 boards that have them, in canvas order, taken from each spec's **Route** and **Motion** fields and checked against the board's inline animation on that view's root (motion.md, "Appendix: every usage"). The generator reads this block (the fenced block tagged `json child-routes`). Per board: `kendali` is the `ShellRoute` controller widget (2.1), `anak` the child routes in order. Per child: `jalur` is the go_router path under `/<Stem>` (path parameters included); `masuk` is the `Kerangka` keyframe of the page transition, `ms` its duration and `kurva` its curve (`keluar` = `PalakatMotion.keluar`, `ease` = `Curves.ease`). `"masuk": null` means no transition; such an entry has no `ms` or `kurva`. Back is instant on every child route (motion.md, "Screen change and page transitions").

### 2.3 Check

Run from the repository root; it prints `ok 199` when the table matches `canvas.json` (count, order, stem, title, page, frame-derived form):

```sh
python3 - <<'PY'
import json,re
c=json.load(open('docs/design/handoff/canvas/canvas.json'))
t=open('docs/build/navigation.md').read().split('### 2.2')[1].split('### 2.3')[0]
rows=[[x.strip() for x in l.strip('|').split(' | ')] for l in t.splitlines() if re.match(r'\| \d+ \|',l)]
def form(b):
  w,h=b['w'],b['h']
  if (w,h)==(390,844): return 'Phone'
  if b.get('expand')=='fill': return 'Laptop' if w==1440 else 'Tablet'
  return 'A4' if {w,h}=={794,1123} else 'Sheet'
assert len(rows)==199==len(c['order'])
for i,(r,f) in enumerate(zip(rows,c['order']),1):
  b=c['boards'][f]; s=f[:-8]
  assert r[0]==str(i) and r[1]==s and r[2]=='`/%s`'%s and r[3]==b['title'].replace('|','\\|') and r[4]==b['page'] and r[5]==form(b), (i,r[:6])
print('ok',len(rows))
PY
```

## 3. Link graph

### 3.1 How to wire a link

```dart
enum Cara { dorong, ganti, naik }

Tautan({required String ke, required Widget child, Cara cara = Cara.dorong, String? label, double radius = 0})

Tautan(ke: 'WebBukti', child: …)                        // push
Tautan(ke: 'Main', cara: Cara.ganti, child: …)          // go
Tautan(ke: 'Lainnya', cara: Cara.naik, child: …)        // up: kembaliKe('/Lainnya')
```

This adds the `cara` parameter to the `Tautan` of components.md 1.6 (which leaves push or go to this file). `Tautan` does nothing when `ke` is the current board. Side-nav, tab-bar and header-back items are `Tautan`s inside `NavSamping`, `PonselTabBar` and `KepalaPonsel`. No board links to a child route of another board: every board-to-board link opens the target board's root route. `ke` may name a child route of the board itself (`'Main/catat'`) for in-board navigation; the screen spec decides those.

The link test (`test/links_test.dart`, README M2) checks coverage, not kinds. `outLinks` in `lib/boards.dart` is generated: manifest `links` ∪ `jsLinks` ∪ the computed links in 3.3, minus self links, minus AIBulan's dead `jsLinks`. `links_test.dart`: expected = `outLinks` from `boards.dart` (navigation.md 3.1). A target is present when the screen file contains `ke: '<T>'`, `kembaliKe: '<T>'` or `keBagi: '<T>'` as a literal, or `item: nav<Name>` whose list contains T, or `PonselTabBar(` (TutupBuku, Lainnya, and Main on lainnya.dart). `ke: '<T>'` covers `Tautan(ke:` and the `ke:` of `Tombol`, `ButirPerhatian` and `KartuKasus`; `kembaliKe:` is the `KepalaPonsel` back arrow; the `nav…` lists are the consts in `lib/shell/nav_item.dart`, which the test imports. Link targets are string literals in the screen file, never only in `lib/mock`. On Lainnya the three tab items that open Main are passed in as `Tautan(ke: 'Main', cara: Cara.ganti)`.

### 3.2 Findings

- **No broken links.** Every target of every link (1282 distinct board-to-board links, including the computed ones) is one of the 199 boards. The manifest's `broken: []` is confirmed.
- **The manifest misses 188 links on 11 boards.** They are built in the logic class from names (`hal('AntreanVerifikasi')`, `l[0] + '.dc.html'`, a `TUJU` table), so the manifest's string scan did not see them: WebTransaksi (4), PetaLayar (100), Cakupan (43), TabTransaksi (4), BerandaJabatan (13), WebBerandaJabatan (9), KotakMasuk (4), WebKotakMasuk (2), CariOrang (4), WebCariOrang (2), AntreanVerifikasi (3). They are real, drawn links. `gen_boards.py` must merge the block in 3.3 into each board's `outLinks`, or the link test will not ask for them.
- **AIBulan's `jsLinks` are dead.** Its logic class defines `navVals()` with the `navKeuangan` list but neither renders a side nav nor calls it. Drop those seven targets from AIBulan's expected links. (The manifest also sets `hasSideNav: true` on phone boards that only share helper code; ignore that flag.)
- **Self links** (kind self) on 27 boards: WebBeranda, WebTransaksi, WebRekonsiliasi, WebTutupBuku, WebPengaturan, WebKewajiban, WebPaketLaporan, WebTerbatas, WebMasuk, WebVerifikasi, WebPemulihan, BerandaJabatan, WebBerandaJabatan, WebPenugasan, WebKotakMasuk, DokumenGereja, WebDokumenGereja, PermohonanSurat, WebPermohonanSurat, Pengumuman, WebPengumuman, WartaArsip, WebWartaArsip, AntreanVerifikasi, WebDataAnggota, PersembahanSaya, KeuanganUnit.
- **No inbound link** (reached only from the launcher): Cakupan, A4F02a, A4F14, A4Sementara, Keputusan, TabTransaksi, TabCatat, PetaPlatform. These have inbound links although the manifest lists none (from PetaLayar, Cakupan or a computed row): WebVerifikasi, WebSambungan, Memuat, WebMemuat, TabBeranda.

### 3.4 Out-links per board

Canvas order. Labels are the visible text, or the `aria-label` of an icon-only link; labels over 70 characters are cut and end in "…"; `{{…}}` is a value the logic class fills. "×n" means the same link appears n times (list rows, header and footer). "row" means a link built in the logic class (list name in brackets). Kinds as in the quick reference. Side-nav and tab-bar items are summarised in one line.

## 4. Launcher

### 4.1 Route and layout

Route `/`, widget `Peluncur`. Its look is components.md 4.10: a laptop-style page without side nav, title "Palakat · prototipe", subtitle "199 layar · data contoh, tanpa server", a `ChipPilihan` "Urutkan menurut" with **"Halaman kanvas"** (default) and **"Perjalanan jabatan"**, and as its first row "Komponen" → `/_komponen`. This section gives what it lists and how its rows navigate.

- A row shows the canvas title and the stem. Tapping it is `Tautan(ke: stem, cara: Cara.ganti)`, so the board opens with the launcher directly below it (2.1).
- The chosen ordering is kept in `PrototypeState` for the session.
- The launcher is the bottom page of every stack; Back from it leaves the app (Android) or goes back in the browser history (web).

## 5. Back, deep links and unknown routes

### 5.1 Back

- **`kembaliKe('/X')`** (kind up): flatten the router's current match list (`GoRouter.of(context).routerDelegate.currentConfiguration`, descending into shell and pushed matches) into the stack of page locations, bottom to top. If the page directly below the current one is `/X` or starts with `/X/`, `context.pop()`; otherwise `context.go('/X')`. Example: Tanggal's back arrow pops to `/Main/catat` when Tanggal was pushed from the Catat form, and does `go('/Main')` when Tanggal was opened from the launcher.
- **Push to a board with child routes that is already in the stack** (2.1, "Re-entering a board with child routes"). Before a `Cara.dorong` push to another board `X`, `Tautan` looks up `ulangPapan['X']`. With no entry it pushes `/X` as usual. With an entry it first captures `GoRouter.of(context)` and the callback (the `Tautan` leaves with its page), then calls `router.pop()` while the top page of the flattened stack is not `/X`, flattening again after each pop, and finally calls the callback. It never pushes or calls `go`. Example: stack `/`, `/Main`, `/Main/transaksi`, `/Cari`; a Cari result row pops `/Cari` and `/Main/transaksi`, resets Main, and leaves `/`, `/Main` showing Beranda in its initial state, so Back returns to the launcher (check 11). Opened from the launcher with no Main below (`/`, `/Cari`), the same row pushes `/Main` and Back returns to Cari (08-cari.md, check 8).
- **System Back (Android) and the browser Back button** pop the top page; at a page reached by `go` they return to the launcher (Android) or to the previous URL (browser history, 5.4). A child route pops to its parent view, as the board's own back does.
- **Open overlays close first.** A board's bottom sheet, side panel, dialog or open "Menu" drawer is state, not a route. While one is open, the screen wraps itself in `PopScope(canPop: false, onPopInvokedWithResult: …)` and Back closes the overlay instead of leaving the page.
- **iOS**: there is no system Back, and `halaman` builds `CustomTransitionPage`/`NoTransitionPage`, which have no edge-swipe back; the board's own back controls remain. PanelKeadaan item 1 also has a "Kembali" action (components.md 4.9), hidden at the launcher. It is the iOS way back from boards without a back control (TutupBuku, Awal, Terbatas list, Pemeriksa, Masuk, PilihBulan; 1.2). It calls `router.routerDelegate.popRoute()`, the call Android Back makes, so it behaves exactly as system Back above: an open overlay closes first, a child route pops to its parent view. Not `maybePop` on the root navigator: TutupBuku, Awal and Terbatas are `ShellRoute` boards whose views and overlay `PopScope`s sit in the nested navigator, which the root navigator's `maybePop` skips.

### 5.2 Frame and panel around the navigator

`MaterialApp.router(builder: (context, child) => BingkaiPerangkat(child: child))`, so the frame wraps the router's navigator, not each page. `BingkaiPerangkat` (components.md 4.8) listens to `router.routerDelegate` and reads the location of the top page from `currentConfiguration` (the last match, resolved through pushed and shell matches); its first path segment is the board stem, looked up in the registry. Then it:

- for a Phone board, on a window wider than 600 with the panel's "Bingkai ponsel" switch on: draws the backdrop and the 390 × 844 frame of components.md 4.8 and lays the navigator out inside it with a `MediaQuery` of 390 × 844, so page transitions run inside the frame and the frame never moves;
- for every other board, the launcher and the not-found page: passes the navigator through full size (A4 and sheet pages draw their own page wrapper);
- always adds `PanelKeadaan` (components.md 4.9, placement there). Its links use `cara: Cara.ganti`: "Semua layar" → `/`; "Tautan masuk" lists every board that links here, from `boards.dart` (the complete inbound set of section 3, not the manifest's).

### 5.3 Transitions

`motion.md` ("Screen change and page transitions") decides these; in short:

- A phone board route enters with `masuk` (opacity 0 → 1, x 24 → 0), `pindahLayar` 280 ms, curve `keluar`, whether reached by push or go.
- Laptop, tablet, A4 and sheet routes: no transition, so the side nav stays still.
- A child route enters with the keyframe its board puts on that view (`masuk`, `naik` for `/Main/mata-anggaran`, `pudar` for tab views), or none.
- Back and pop are instant everywhere; the page underneath does not replay its entrance.
- Reduce motion on (system or panel): every transition is instant.

### 5.4 Web URLs and deep links

- Hash URLs (Flutter's default; do not call `usePathUrlStrategy`), so the release build works from any static server without rewrites: `http://localhost:8080/#/WebBukti`, `…/#/Main/catat`.
- Set `GoRouter.optionURLReflectsImperativeAPIs = true` before creating the router, so a push shows its own URL in the address bar and adds a browser history entry; browser Back then pops it and Forward pushes it again.
- Opening any board URL directly builds the launcher below it (2.1); a child route URL builds launcher, parent, child. Every route renders with the board's initial state and the tweak values currently in `PrototypeState` (defaults after a reload).
- A child route opened directly whose view needs earlier steps follows its spec (for example 02-awal.md redirects `/Awal/saldo` to `/Awal` unless Bendahara authority is active). Without such a rule, the child view renders with the board's initial state. A path parameter that names no record (`/Kewajiban/kasus/:id`, `/Laporan/rinci/:f`, `/Terbatas/transaksi/:no`) redirects to the board's root route.
- Query strings are ignored. A reload loses all state (CONVENTIONS: nothing persists).

### 5.5 Unknown route

`errorBuilder` shows `TidakDitemukanScreen` (prototype chrome, fluid, tokens): heading "Layar tidak ditemukan", the requested path in mono 13 `tinta3`, and a primary button "Semua layar" → `go('/')`. Case matters: `/main`, `/Main.dc.html` and `/Main/xyz` are all unknown.

### 5.6 Checks for M2

1. `/` lists 199 boards under "Halaman kanvas" in the order of 4.2, plus "Komponen"; "Perjalanan jabatan" shows the 8 roles of 4.3.
2. From the launcher open WebPaketLaporan, press "Daftar Bukti Kas" → URL `#/WebBukti`; breadcrumb "Laporan" pops back to `#/WebPaketLaporan`; browser Back from WebBukti does the same.
3. Open `#/WebBukti` directly; breadcrumb "Laporan" does `go('/WebPaketLaporan')`; browser Back returns to `#/WebBukti`; Android Back from WebPaketLaporan returns to the launcher.
4. Side nav at 1440: item "Rekonsiliasi" on WebBeranda → `#/WebRekonsiliasi`, no transition, active item moves. At 860 and 390: only the top bar and "Menu"; "Menu" opens the list and footer, reads "Tutup menu"; choosing an item navigates and the new page starts closed.
5. Main tab bar: "Bulan" → `/TutupBuku` (go); Back returns to the launcher on Android and to `/Main` in the browser. On Lainnya, "Transaksi" opens `/Main` at Beranda.
6. Phone push Main → Cari ("Cari") enters with `masuk` inside the device frame at 1440 wide; the frame does not move; Back is instant; with reduce motion the entrance is instant too.
7. Main → Catat form (`/Main/catat`) → Tanggal (push) → back arrow pops to `/Main/catat` with the form still filled.
8. Masuk "Buka Beranda" (go) → Main; Back does not return to Masuk.
9. `#/Nope` and `#/main` show "Layar tidak ditemukan" with a working "Semua layar".
10. A bottom sheet open on Main: system Back closes the sheet, Main stays.
11. `/Main` → `/Main/transaksi` → Cari → row → `/Main` shows Main Beranda with fresh state, no exception, and Back returns to the launcher.

Not covered here: the Keadaan panel's contents beyond its links (CONVENTIONS), tweak behaviour (screens specs), the look of each screen (screens specs, components.md).
